Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 60, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

Do not take My enemy and your enemy: that is, the disbelievers and polytheists.

As allies, showing them affection: that is, do not take them as helpers to whom you show love.

And they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth: that is, Islam in creed and law.

They expel the Messenger and you: that is, by oppressing you until you left, fleeing with your religion.

Because you believed in your Lord: that is, because you believed in your Lord.

If you have gone out in struggle in My cause and seeking My pleasure: then do not take them as allies, nor exchange affection with them.

You send them affection secretly: that is, you convey to them, in a covert manner, news of the Messenger's going out to fight them.

And whoever of you does that: that is, whoever shows affection to them and so passes on to them the secrets of the Prophet in his wars and other matters.

Then he has certainly strayed from the even way: that is, he has erred from the path of truth, the straight road that leads to happiness.

If they overcome you: that is, if they gain the upper hand over you, having power over you in some place.

They will be enemies to you: that is, they will not acknowledge any affection toward you.

And extend their hands against you: that is, with beating and killing.

And their tongues with evil: that is, with abuse and insult.

And they wish you would disbelieve: that is, they desire that you would disbelieve in your religion and your Prophet and return to polytheism with them.

Your relatives will not benefit you, nor your children: that is, if you show affection to them and send them news of war, seeking closeness to them so that they will spare your relatives and children among them, then know that your relatives and children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection.

On the Day of Resurrection He will separate between you: that is, you will be in Paradise, and the polytheists, among them your children and relatives, will be in the Fire.

Explanation of the verses:

The opening of this surah, ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ to the end of the verses, was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who was among the emigrants who witnessed Badr. Muslim reported in his Sahih, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad, and said: "Go to Rawdat Khakh (a place between it and Medina at a distance of twelve miles), for there is a woman traveling (a female traveler) with a letter; take it from her." So we set off, urging our horses on, that is, making them hasten. Suddenly we came upon a woman, and we said: "Bring out the letter." She said: "I have no letter with me." We said: "You will certainly bring out the letter, or we will strip you of your clothes (that is, from upon you)." So she brought it out from her braids, that is, from the plaits of her hair, and we brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Behold, it was from Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to some of the polytheists of Mecca, informing them of some matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Hatib, what is this?" He said: "Do not hasten against me, O Messenger of Allah. I was a man attached to Quraysh (that is, he was an ally of Quraysh and not a Qurashi), and those of the emigrants who are with you have relatives by whom they protect their families. I wished, since I missed that lineage, to make for myself a hand among them by which they would protect my kin. I did not do it out of disbelief, nor apostasy from my religion, nor contentment with disbelief after Islam. I knew that Allah would send His punishment upon them, that my letter would not avail them anything against Allah, and that Allah would give you victory over them."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "He has spoken the truth." Then Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He witnessed Badr. What would make you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿do not take My enemy and your enemy﴾ from the disbelievers and polytheists ﴿as allies﴾, that is, as helpers, ﴿showing them affection﴾, that is, the secrets of the Prophet ﷺ concerning war, which are of great import and consequence. While they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, which is the religion of Islam with its creed, its law, its Book and its Messenger. They expel the Messenger and you from your homes by oppressing you until you emigrated, fleeing with your religion, ﴿because you believed in your Lord﴾, that is, because you believed in your Lord. Do you take these disbelievers, these wrongdoers, as allies, sending them affection?.. Indeed, this is a grave error on the part of whoever does this.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you have gone out in struggle in My cause and seeking My pleasure﴾, that is, if you have gone out from your homes as strivers in My cause, to support My religion, My Messenger, and My believing allies, and seeking My approval, then do not take the disbelievers as allies apart from Me, showing them affection.

And His saying, exalted is He, "You send them affection secretly," that is, you conceal affection for them by conveying the secret news of the Messenger, while I am ﴿more knowing﴾ than you and than others ﴿of what you conceal and what you reveal﴾. And indeed I have informed My Messenger of your letter sent to the polytheists of Mecca, which contains the exposure of the secret of My Messenger concerning his resolve to fight them by surprise, so that he might conquer Mecca without much shedding of blood and taking of lives.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever of you does that﴾, that is, shows loyalty and affection to the polytheists, ﴿has certainly strayed from the even way﴾, that is, has erred from the middle of the path safe from deviation, which leads toward the true Islam.

And His saying: ﴿If they overcome you, they will be enemies to you and extend their hands and tongues against you with evil, and they wish you would disbelieve﴾, that is, they are truly your enemies. If they overcome you, that is, gain the upper hand over you, having power over you, they will be enemies to you and will not care for your affection toward them, and they will extend their hands to you with beating and killing, and their tongues with abuse and insult, and they wish for your disbelief so that you return to polytheism like them.

And His saying: ﴿Your relatives will not benefit you, nor your children﴾ whom you showed affection to the disbelievers for the sake of, from the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter, since Hatib wrote the letter for the sake of his relatives and children; thus Allah, exalted is He, made clear the error of Hatib in that.

And His saying: ﴿On the Day of Resurrection He will separate between you﴾, by making you, O believers, in Paradise, and your relatives and children who are polytheists in the Fire. So what benefit then is there in disobedience for their sake?! And Allah is seeing of what you do, so be watchful of Him and beware Him, and do not step outside His obedience and the obedience of His Messenger.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The prohibition of allying with disbelievers through support, backing and affection, in preference to the Muslims.

2- Whoever conveys the military secrets of the Muslims to the disbelievers is in grave danger, even if he fasts and prays.

3- A clarification that disbelievers do not show mercy to the believers whenever they gain power over them, for their hearts are blind, not knowing good nor evil, due to the darkness of disbelief within their souls, and their lack of awareness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since they do not know Him nor believe in what is with Him of bliss and torment on the Day of Resurrection.

4- The virtue of the people of Badr and their honor with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

5- Acceptance of the excuse of sincere, righteous people who were early in Islam, when one of them slips through ijtihad (independent reasoning) on his part.

6- A person's relatives will not benefit him on the Day of Resurrection if he is a Muslim and they are disbelievers.

**Explanation of the Words (Sharh al-Kalimat)**

*Qad kana lakum*: that is, O believers.

*Uswatun hasanah*: that is, a good example.

*Fi Ibrahim wa'lladhina ma'ahu*: from among the believers; so follow them.

*Idh qalu li-qawmihim*: that is, the polytheists.

*Inna bura'u minkum wa-mimma ta'buduna min duni'llah*: that is, we disown you and what you worship besides Allah, namely your idols which you worship.

*Kafarna bikum*: that is, we denied you, and we did not acknowledge any kinship or loyalty to you.

*Wa-bada bayninā wa-baynakumu'l-'adawatu wa'l-baghda'*: that is, this became manifest and clear, with no ambiguity or concealment.

*Hatta tu'minu billahi wahdah*: that is, our enmity and hatred toward you will continue until you believe in Allah alone.

*Wa-ilayka anabna*: that is, we have turned back to You in all our affairs.

*Rabbana la taj'alna fitnatan lilladhina kafaru*: that is, do not let them prevail over us, so that they tempt us in our religion and are themselves tempted by us, thinking they are upon the truth because they overcome us.

*Laqad kana lakum fihim uswatun hasanah*: that is, there has indeed been for you, O believers, a good example in Ibrahim and those with him.

*Liman kana yarju'llaha wa'l-yawma'l-akhir*: that is, this is a good example for whoever believes in Allah and hopes for what is with Him on the Day of Resurrection.

*Wa-man yatawalla*: that is, whoever does not accept the guidance we gave him regarding faith and patience, and returns to disbelief.

*Fa-inna'llaha ghaniyyun hamid*: that is, Allah has no need of his faith and patience; He is self-sufficient, not in need of anything else, and *hamid* means praiseworthy for His bounties and His favours to His servants.

**The Meaning of the Verses (Ma'na al-Ayat)**

When the Exalted forbade the believers to take the disbelievers as allies, even though there may be a need that calls for such alliance, as occurred in the excuse of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, He wished to encourage them to oppose the disbelievers and not to ally with them under any circumstances, because of the harm and danger that this poses to their creed and their bond with Allah, which is the most precious thing that believers possess. He informed them that there is for them an *uswah* (good example), i.e., a fine model, in Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah, and in the believers with him. Despite their small number, the great number of their enemies, their weakness and the strength of their opponents, they disowned the enemies of Allah and repudiated any tie that bound them to them. They said what Allah related of them in His words: ﴿Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah﴾ — namely, idols and images. *Kafarna bikum* — we denied you, so we did not acknowledge any existence that would require our affection and support for you. *Wa-bada* — there became manifest between us and you the enmity and hatred in an open form with no cover over it, because we are monotheists and you are polytheists, because we are believers and you are disbelievers. This enmity and hatred will continue between us and you until you believe in Allah alone as Lord and God, with no lord other than Him and no god besides Him. Therefore, O Muslims, take as your example the leader of the monotheists, Ibrahim — except for the forgiveness Ibrahim sought for his father, which you should not follow. You should not seek forgiveness for your dead polytheists, for Ibrahim abandoned that when he knew that his father would not believe, that he would die a disbeliever, and that he was in the Fire. Thus the Exalted said, excepting the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "Azar": ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power to obtain anything for you from Allah﴾, i.e., beyond seeking forgiveness.

This was in accordance with a promise he had made to him at the time of parting, when he said in Surah Maryam: ﴿He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me."﴾ [Verse: 47]. And in Surah al-Tawbah the Exalted said: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him.﴾ [Verse: 114].

And His words: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned back in repentance﴾, i.e., we have returned from disbelief to faith in You and to affirming Your oneness in worship. ﴿And to You is the destination﴾, i.e., the final return of all things is to You, and they end with You, so You decree and judge as You will. ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers﴾, i.e., do not let them prevail over us, lest they tempt us in our religion and turn us back to disbelief, and lest they be tempted by us, thinking that because they have overcome us they are upon the truth and we upon falsehood, so that they increase in disbelief and do not believe.

﴿And forgive us, our Lord﴾, i.e., our past and future sins, so do not hold us accountable for them. ﴿Indeed, You are the Almighty, the Exalted in Might, the Avenger against whoever disobeys You, the All-Wise in Your management of Your allies.﴾ So manage for us that which benefits us and pleases You with regard to us. This supplication and humble entreaty, from His words ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied﴾ to ﴿the All-Wise﴾, may possibly be what Ibrahim and the believers with him said, or it may be a guidance from Allah to the believers that they should say it, to strengthen their faith and to make them firm in it, as Ibrahim and those with him did. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 60, verses 7–9:

Explanation of the words:

ʿādaytum minhum (you have shown enmity toward them): that is, from the disbelievers of Quraysh in Makkah, in obedience to Allah and compliance with His command.

Mawaddah (affection): that is, love and loyalty, by Allah guiding them to faith and Islam, so that they believe, submit, and become your allies.

Wa-llahu qadir (and Allah is able): that is, able to do this, and He has done it, for after the conquest the people of Makkah embraced Islam, except a few of them.

Lam yuqatilukum fi'l-din (they did not fight you over religion): that is, for the sake of religion.

An tabarruhum (that you be kind to them): that is, that you do good to them.

Wa-tuqsitu ilayhim (and deal justly with them): that is, that you be equitable toward them and act fairly with them.

Inna Allaha yuhibbu al-muqsitin (indeed Allah loves those who act justly): that is, those who are fair and just in their judgments and in those under their authority.

Wa-zaharuʿala ikhrajikum (and helped against your expulsion): that is, they aided and supported the enemy in driving you out of your homes.

An tawallawhum (that you take them as allies): that is, that you befriend them with support and love.

Fa-ulaʾika humu al-zalimun (then those are the wrongdoers): because they have placed loyalty in other than its proper place, and injustice is placing a thing other than its proper place.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to explain the ruling on allegiance to disbelievers. When Allah prohibited that, and the believers had disbelieving relatives, and in obedience to their faith and their response to the call of their Lord they severed ties with them, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave them good news in this noble verse that He is able to place affection between them and their relatives. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿It may be that Allah will place affection between you and those among them with whom you have been at enmity﴾, that is, among the polytheists, ﴿affection﴾. This is by guiding them to Islam, and He is able to do that, and He has done it, and to Him belongs praise and favor. Allah opened Makkah to His Messenger, and its people believed, except a few, so affection came about, and loyalty and brotherhood, in confirmation of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "It may be that Allah will place affection between you and those among them with whom you have been at enmity. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." He forgave them, having turned to them after guiding them, and pardoned them for the sins that had come from them, and showed them mercy.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾, that is, He does not restrict you from being kind to them with food, clothing, or conveyance, and from acting justly toward them by being fair to them. This applies in every time and place and to all disbelievers, but on the conditions that Allah mentioned, which are:

First: that they do not fight us for the sake of our religion.

Second: that they do not expel us from our homes by oppressing us and forcing us to emigrate.

Third: that they do not aid any of our enemies with any assistance, even with counsel and opinion, let alone with mounts and weapons.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ is an encouragement to them toward justice and fairness, even with a disbeliever. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He only forbids you﴾ from allegiance to those who fought you over religion, expelled you from your homes, and aided [others] ﴿in your expulsion, that you make allies of them﴾, that is, He forbids you from allying with them. ﴿And whoever allies with them﴾ among you, turning away from this divine guidance and this Lord's command, ﴿those are the wrongdoers﴾, that is, wrongdoers against themselves, who expose themselves to Allah's punishment and wrath, because they placed loyalty in other than its proper place after they had come to know and understand this.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of the ruling on forbidden and permitted allegiance in Islam.

2- Encouragement toward justice and fairness, after they were obligatory, to help one stand firm in upholding them.

3- Affirmation of what the scholars said: that "ʿasā" (it may be) from Allah indicates that what is hoped for by it will certainly occur and come into being, unlike when it comes from other than Allah, where it expresses hope and expectation, and what is hoped for may or may not occur.

﴿When the believing women come to you as emigrants﴾: that is, the believing women, by their tongues, emigrating from the disbelievers.

﴿Then test them﴾: that is, examine them by having them swear that they did not leave except out of desire for Islam, not out of hatred for their husbands, nor out of love for men among the Muslims.

﴿And if you know them to be believers﴾: that is, sincere in their faith according to their oath.

﴿Then do not return them to the disbelievers﴾: that is, do not send them back to the disbelievers in Makkah.

﴿They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾: the believing women are not lawful to their disbelieving husbands, and the disbelievers are not lawful to their believing wives.

﴿And give them what they have spent﴾: that is, give the disbelieving husbands of the emigrant believing women the bridal gifts that they had given to their wives.

﴿And there is no blame upon you for marrying them when you have given them their due compensation﴾: that is, their bridal gifts, even if no divorce has taken place from their husbands, since the contract is dissolved by Islam; and after the completion of the waiting period for one who has been consummated with, and the remaining conditions of marriage.

﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾: that is, your wives, since your Islam severs the marital bond. Likewise one who apostatizes and joins the abode of disbelief, unless she returns to Islam before her waiting period ends, in which case her marriage is not annulled and the bond remains, if she was consummated with.

﴿And ask for what you have spent﴾: that is, demand what you spent on them as bridal gifts in the case of apostasy.

﴿And let them ask for what they have spent﴾: that is, the bridal gifts they spent on the emigrant women in the case of their conversion to Islam.

﴿And if any of your wives escape you to the disbelievers﴾: that is, if the wife of one of you flees to the disbelievers, joins them, and they do not give you her bridal gift, and then you retaliate against the disbelievers and take spoils from them.

﴿Then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾: that is, give those whose wives went to the disbelievers the equivalent of what they had spent on them as bridal gifts.

﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾: that is, fear Allah, in whom you believe, by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ (verses 10 and 11): these two verses were revealed after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, since the terms of the treaty included that any man who came to the Messenger ﷺ from Makkah would be returned to Makkah even if he was a Muslim, and whoever came to the polytheists from Madinah would not be returned to him. The treaty did not specify women. In the course of this, Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt came as an emigrant from Makkah to Madinah, and her two brothers, 'Ammarah and al-Walid, followed her to return her to Quraysh. Then this noble verse was revealed, and the Messenger ﷺ did not return her to them. Allah, the Exalted, says ﴿O you who have believed﴾: that is, O you who have believed in Allah as Lord and God, and in Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and in Islam as religion, ﴿when the believing women come to you as emigrants from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam, then test them — Allah knows best their faith — and if you know them, that is, if it becomes evident to your assumption that they are believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers.﴾ The form of the test is that she be told: swear by Allah, that is, say by Allah, there is no god but Him, that you did not leave except out of desire for Islam, not out of hatred for my husband, nor out of love for a Muslim man.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾: because Islam has dissolved that marital bond which existed between the husband and his wife, since Allah has forbidden marriage to polytheist women and the giving of believing women in marriage to polytheist men. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, did not permit their return to their disbelieving husbands.

As for the words of Allah, ﴿And give them what they have spent﴾: when their polytheist husband comes demanding it, you shall give him what he spent on her as bridal gift, and the one who gives it is the community of the Muslims and their leader.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And there is no blame upon you for marrying them﴾: that is, you may marry them when you have given them their due compensation, that is, their bridal gifts, along with the remaining conditions of marriage: a guardian, two witnesses, and the completion of the waiting period for one who has been consummated with.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾: that is, if a man becomes Muslim while his wife remains a polytheist, the marital bond is severed and she becomes unlawful to her husband who has embraced Islam. Likewise, if a Muslim woman apostatizes and joins the abode of disbelief, the bond is severed, and it is not lawful to hold on to her. The benefit of this is that if a man had several wives, he may take a fourth, because the wife who apostatized, or the wife who was a polytheist and whose husband became Muslim while she was still in his marriage, does not prevent him from marrying a fourth, since Islam has severed the bond, by the saying of Allah, ﴿do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾. ("al-'Isam" is the plural of "'ismah".)

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And ask for what you have spent﴾: demand from the apostate woman the bridal gift that you spent on her, which is to be paid to you; ﴿and let them ask for what they have spent﴾: and give them also the bridal gifts of their wives who embraced Islam and emigrated to you. And the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of His creation and their needs, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His decree and His management; so let the judgment be accepted for Him, and let one be content with it, for it is founded upon the basis of the interest of all.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And if any of your wives escape you to the disbelievers, and you then retaliate﴾: that is, if some of your wives go to the disbelievers as apostates, and you demand the bridal gifts but they do not give them to you, then you fight and take spoils, then give from the booty before its division to the one whose wife went to the abode of disbelief and who did not receive compensation, the equivalent of what he spent.

As for His words: ﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾: that is, fear His punishment, so obey Him in His commands and prohibitions, and do not disobey Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to test the emigrant woman. If her Islam is known, it is not lawful to return her to her disbelieving husband, since she is not lawful to him, and he is to be given what he spent on her as bridal gift. After that it is permissible to marry her with a bridal gift, a guardian and two witnesses; if she was consummated with, then after the completion of her waiting period, and otherwise there is no blame in marrying her immediately.

2- The prohibition of marrying a polytheist woman.

3- It is not permissible to keep in marriage a polytheist wife. The Muslim husband whose wife remained in disbelief, or apostatized after her Islam, may demand what he spent on her as bridal gift, and the disbelieving husband whose wife embraced Islam and emigrated may likewise ask for what he spent on her.

4- If a man's wife has gone and he has not been repaid anything of what he spent on her, and then the Muslims raid those lands and take spoils, then the man whose wife went shall be given what he spent from the booty before its division. If there is no booty, the community of Muslims and their leader shall assist him with part of what he spent, as a matter of mutual solidarity and cooperation.

5- The obligation to fear Allah by implementing His law, enforcing His rulings, and being content with them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 60, verses 12–13:

Explanation of the words:

﴿إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك﴾: That is, on the day of the Conquest (Fath), while the Messenger ﷺ was sitting on al-Safa and ʿUmar was below him.

﴿فبايعهن﴾: That is, on condition that they not associate anything with Allah, and that they not disobey you in what is right.

﴿أن لا يشركن بالله﴾: That is, any kind of shirk or associates.

﴿ولا يقتلن أولادهن﴾: That is, as the people of jahiliyyah used to kill their daughters by burying them alive.

﴿ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه﴾: That is, a lie they fabricate, such as bringing a foundling child and attributing it to the husband when it is not his child.

﴿ولا يعصينك في معروف﴾: That is, whatever the Shariʿah recognizes as good and sound, which he commanded and urged; or whatever the Shariʿah recognizes as forbidden and reprehensible.

﴿فبايعهن﴾: That is, accept their pledge of allegiance.

﴿واستغفر لهن الله﴾: That is, ask Allah, exalted is He, to forgive them for the sins they committed in the past and those they may yet commit.

﴿قوماً غضب الله عليهم﴾: That is, the Jews.

﴿قد يئسوا من الآخرة﴾: That is, from its reward, despite their certainty of it, and that is due to their obstinacy towards the Prophet while knowing his truthfulness.

﴿كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور﴾: That is, like the despair of those before them among the Jews who disbelieved in ʿIsa and died in that state; they too have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿يٰأيُّها ٱلنَّبِيُّ﴾ up to His saying ﴿إنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾: This is the verse of the pledge of allegiance of women. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the pledge from the women of Quraysh on the day of the Conquest while he was sitting on al-Safa and ʿUmar was below him, lower than him, taking the pledge. They asked him to extend his hand, and he said: "I do not shake hands with women. I take their pledge that they will not associate anything with Allah, that is, any kind of shirk or associates, and that they will not steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children as the women of jahiliyyah used to bury their daughters, nor bring a slander which they fabricate, that is, a lie they invent before their hands and feet, meaning that they will not attribute to their husbands children who are not theirs, and that they will not disobey you in what is right." This is in general, and in particular concerning wailing (niyahah), for the women in jahiliyyah used to wail over the dead, tear their garments, and scratch their faces. Allah, exalted is He, said: O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you, then accept their pledge that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring a slander they fabricate between their hands and feet, nor disobey you in what is right. So accept their pledge and ask Allah to forgive them for what has passed of their sins and what may yet come. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿يٰأيُّها ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾: That is, O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry, namely the Jews. Do not befriend them with support and affection. ﴿وقد يئسوا من الآخرة﴾: That is, they have despaired of Allah's reward in it, of entering Paradise, because of their obstinacy towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and their disbelief in him, despite knowing that he is the Messenger of Allah. Whoever disbelieves in him, denies him, or opposes and fights him will not enter Paradise; therefore they are despairing of entering Paradise.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿كَما يَئِسَ ٱلْكُفّارُ مِن أصْحابِ ٱلْقُبُورِ﴾: That is, just as their brethren who died before them despaired of entering Paradise, having disbelieved in ʿIsa, peace be upon him, and fought him and his mother, and accused ʿIsa of sorcery and his mother of unchastity, may Allah protect us. Thus these despair of entering Paradise just as those among them who died have despaired, and they are the people of the graves.

Guidance from the verses

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The legitimacy of taking the pledge of allegiance for the leader of the Muslims, and the obligation to fulfil it.

2- The prohibition of shirk and what is mentioned with it: theft, adultery, killing children, lying, slander, and attributing a child to other than his father.

3- The prohibition of wailing and what is mentioned with it: tearing garments, scratching faces, and speaking with non-mahram men.

4- The free woman is far removed from adultery. Hind said while pledging: "Does a free woman commit adultery?" He said: "A free woman does not commit adultery."

5- The prohibition of women shaking hands with men, based on his saying ﷺ in the pledge: "I do not shake hands with women."

6- The prohibition of allying with the Jews through support and affection.
